bug_semantics: When a broker has a network connector with syncDurableSubs=true, TransportConnection.processBrokerInfo() treats an inbound OpenWire BrokerInfo (networkConnection=true) as a durable-sync request and immediately dispatchSync()s a BrokerSubscriptionInfo that enumerates every durable topic subscription on the broker (copied ConsumerInfo: clientId, subscriptionName, destination, JMS selector). That reply is sent as soon as BrokerInfo is processed, before ConnectionInfo is run through broker.addConnection() and the authentication plugin chain. An unauthenticated attacker who can reach the OpenWire port therefore spoofs a network-bridge BrokerInfo and receives the full durable-subscription metadata set.
flaw_origin: AMQ-6373 (2016-07-20) added OpenWire v12 BrokerSubscriptionInfo and wired processBrokerInfo to dump all durable subs whenever the peer's BrokerInfo networkProperties parsed syncDurableSubs=true. The new non-duplex branch (and the matching duplex branch) performed that dump with no check that the connection had authenticated. Authentication lives on the later ConnectionInfo path; the feature never gated the reply on that path. Default syncDurableSubs is false, matching the CVE's AC:H configuration precondition. A later AMQ-6472 helper move to NetworkBridgeUtils.getBrokerSubscriptionInfo() is a refactor of the enumerator, not a new leak.

reasoning: CVE-2026-49270 is a real, unwithdrawn information-disclosure bug: an unauthenticated OpenWire BrokerInfo can elicit BrokerSubscriptionInfo listing every durable topic subscription when syncDurableSubs is enabled. The mechanism first appears in 3953b9aaefaee914bdd0702f27aef47c021ceb27 (AMQ-6373, 2016-07-20): processBrokerInfo newly responds to network BrokerInfo by dispatching a full durable-sub dump, with no authentication gate. Immediate parent a65f5e7c2077e048a2664339f6425d73948d71ce has neither BrokerSubscriptionInfo nor any syncDurableSubs reply path, so the leak is absent there. git log -L on the surviving 6.2.5 leak lines names 3953b9aae as the first write; AMQ-6472 only relocated the enumerator helper and is not a BIC. The commit is a single-parent 2016 feature landing (not a squash/move/revert). It is an ancestor of activemq-5.14.0 (name-rev tags/activemq-5.14.0~25) and not of 5.13.5, matching the CNA affected-from. The security fix first landed on main as b6f9a14e1a6ad1b9a3f1c41eb5ea2db990eaba34 (PR #2047, 2026-05-27), delaying the dump until ConnectionInfo has successfully passed broker.addConnection(); equivalent backports #2048/#2049 sit immediately under the 6.2.6 and 5.19.7 tags.
